review_basis: Frozen report input, grounded element statements, formal plan, deterministic P/I/V AST, validation output and solver output. Z3 success was not treated as semantic correctness.

rating_scale.pass: faithful to the report and correctly scoped
rating_scale.partial: core direction is correct but a material condition, scope or observable relation is weakened or omitted
rating_scale.fail: misclassified, contradicted, circular or missing a critical report condition
rating_scale.not_evaluable: the pipeline did not emit the corresponding final artifact

semantic_live2_target_observations.assumption_numeric_relief: verified: zero narrative-assumption rejections (live1 had two; both gate firings this batch were correct bound/self-comparison catches)
semantic_live2_target_observations.rate_restatement_rule: not exercised: no report in this batch defines a rate quantity
semantic_live2_target_observations.i_applicability_scope_rule: held in the three candidates: conditions carry the report's general qualifiers, no subcase narrowing recurred

summary.interpretation: Engineering completion rose to 3/5 with all candidates offline-verified through run-directory prompt snapshots, and the element layer stayed clean (5/5 P/I/V, zero post-action observations in P). The assumption_numeric_relief fix is verified: zero narrative-assumption rejections (live1 had two) while both numeric-gate firings this batch were correct catches. The I applicability-scope rule held in all three candidates; the rate rule was not exercised by this batch. The two rejections share one formalization-stage family: the first attempts were correctly rejected (self-comparison placeholder, Boolean-hidden bound), the repairs pointed in the right direction but were discarded for touching the frozen pattern field, and offline replay shows they would still fail the numeric gate because explicit bounds were expressed as a non-literal constant (2^12 vs bit-range text) and as a symbol instead of the literal 1. This is an assistant review on n=5, not an expert gold standard or population accuracy estimate, and it is not comparable to earlier batches because the report sets are disjoint.

ratings.reason: The three preconditions are pre-action facts (owner's window signature structure, validity bytes outside the signed digest, interceptable UserOp) with the attacker kept general (bundler, relayer, or anyone). The intent and impacts are faithful. temporal_validity fits. Formula P encodes the window ordering and the two enabling facts before execution; the relation is the full owner-window obligation (execution between validAfter and validUntil) rather than a scenario subcase; V is P with execution outside the window. Ambiguities honestly record that no real manipulated transaction was observed.

P is two pre-action conditions (order posted, same-price order already exists). The intent and the zero-pointer impact are faithful, and state_correspondence is a reasonable class. Formula V (P with both prevOrderId and nextOrderId zero) matches the report's direct observable. Formula I weakens the stated consistency requirement to pointer non-zeroness: non-zero pointers are necessary but not sufficient for a correctly linked list, and no report fragment grounds the correct neighbor identities, so a stronger faithful encoding was not constructible -- direction correct, observable weakened.

P is three pre-action protocol facts (immutable constructor-captured DOMAIN_SEPARATOR, chainid changed by fork/upgrade, non-upgradeable contract) with no post-action observation. The intent (signature validation should survive a chainid change) and impacts (recover always fails, deposits bricked) are faithful, and progress_or_liveness fits a DoS. Formula P is the conjunction of the three facts; the relation is recover_failed == false, the unweakened functional requirement; V is P with recover_failed, matching the selected impact. Ambiguities honestly record the conditional (no observed incident) nature.

Elements are faithful: multi-leg TokenId structure and bit layout are protocol facts, and the intent (width() isolates the lower 12 bits) and impacts are correct. The first plan was correctly rejected for a trivial self-comparison placeholder (stored_width == stored_width). The repair chose the right direction but two blockers remain, confirmed by offline replay of the saved retry plan: fixing the predicate requires modifying pattern, which field-scoped repair freezes, and the repaired bound stored_width < 4096 is not a literal of the report text (the report states the width as bit range [36:48), 12-bit semantics), so the numeric gate would still reject it. Remaining failure is formalization-stage constant-expression, not element or prompt-rule failure.

Elements are faithful: CL gauge type with the explicit _gaugeType == 1 bound, a fake pool exposing whitelisted tokens, attacker veNFT power, factory-validation intent and gauge-creation impact. The first plan hid the explicit bound behind a truth Boolean, correctly rejected by the numeric gate. The repair restored an explicit comparison but expressed the bound as a symbol (gauge_type == cl_gauge_type_constant) rather than the report's literal constant 1, and also needed pattern changes frozen by field-scoped repair; offline replay confirms the repaired plan still fails the bound check. Same formalization-stage constant-expression family as Panoptic.
